s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage in one eye
Presence of glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals floating in the aqueous
key_facts: Patient is a young girl
Right eye is blind
Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina was observed
Chronic retinal detachment was found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Eales disease
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage with retinal detachment

shortlist.label: Retinal detachment
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic retinal detachment found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Intraocular inflammation possible cause of hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage

raw.rationale: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor and a morning glory optic disc anomaly, along with spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage, are characteristic of Eales disease.

rejected.label: Retinal detachment
rejected.why: While retinal detachment is present, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains all key facts, including the presence of crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Vitreous hemorrhage
rejected.why: Vitreous hemorrhage is a symptom rather than a diagnosis that explains all key facts.

rejected.label: Hyphema
rejected.why: Hyphema is a symptom rather than a diagnosis that explains all key facts.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: Uveitis does not typically present with iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor or a morning glory optic disc anomaly.
